criteria.text: POST /agent-sessions with agentId='secretary' resolves the real Secretary profile's allowed_mcps_json before creating the opencode session, passes the resulting mcpRoleConfig to the initial opencodeClient.createSession call, and the RESOLVED MCP TOOL SET of the created fork session excludes servers not allowed by that profile (verified by feeding the real wire-level mcpAllowlist through the fork's real filterMcpToolsByAllowlist), and persists the effective mcp_role and mcp_allowed_tools_json on the Rhythm session.
criteria.test_id: issue-765-c1: the resolved MCP tool set of the created Secretary session EXCLUDES disallowed servers
criteria.note: End-to-end: real OpencodeClientService.createSession (via __setTestClient seam) runs real expandMcpAllowlist; the captured body.mcpAllowlist is filtered through the FORK's real filterMcpToolsByAllowlist against a multi-server catalog. Falsifiability proven: removing the controller profile-scope branch turns the resolved-tool-set assertion RED (gmail/pco tools appear).

criteria.text: POST /agent-sessions for a profile with no allowed_mcps_json remains unrestricted and does not invent an MCP role or allowlist.
criteria.test_id: issue-765-c2: a profile with no allowed_mcps_json stays unrestricted — all servers resolve

criteria.text: An explicit mcpRole in the POST /agent-sessions request takes precedence over the agent profile's allowed_mcps_json.
criteria.test_id: issue-765-c3: an explicit mcpRole in the request overrides the profile allowlist
criteria.note: Precedence asserted on the persisted mcp_role: the explicit role wins over the profile-derived 'secretary'. Guarded to run only when a .mcp-roles/*.mcp.json file is resolvable in the checkout.
